claimBlocks.text: The NPS overview describes descendant knowledge alongside archival research in locating and interpreting Sand Creek. Its short orientation provides a starting point for public history, rather than a complete account of the 1864 attack or its aftermath. The linked individual testimony and media were not inspected for this collection.

claimBlocks.suggestedSection: A dated framework for collaborative public history
claimBlocks.text: The December 2017 foundation document identifies tribal histories and consultation as important to interpreting the site. Its planning entries call for further community involvement and review of research. These are dated institutional priorities and identified needs, not proof that proposed projects were completed. They do not establish a single position shared by every Arapaho government or person.

Alexa Roberts describes the Northern Arapaho Tribe choosing to conduct its part of the 1999 oral-history project internally. Her account explains why participation and control of research materials mattered, while describing different arrangements with Cheyenne communities. This is evidence about a particular collaborative process. The underlying recordings, interviews and photographs were not accessed or reproduced, and their permissions are not Atlas reuse rights.

researchNotes: Old NPS CRM route returned 404. The current official bibliography links the independent NPSHistory archive; actual article downloaded through ordinary validated HTTPS. No access controls bypassed.
The NPS foundation and Roberts paper are distinct works; the brief NPS story page remains supporting. No casualty totals, restricted narratives, precise sites or source media reproduced.
